requirements.requirement: node3 (lan-a) can open an HTTP connection to node4:8080 through the double-NAT transit path
requirements.summary: cmd-3b8a5fadf5f64cba shows a successful curl GET from node3 to node4:8080 returning HTTP/1.0 200 OK with the expected body. cmd-6a87cc71aa8740a9 confirms node4's own HTTP access log recorded this connection.

requirements.requirement: First SNAT hop occurs on node1 (VyOS) as traffic from lan-a enters the transit network
requirements.summary: cmd-29510caccf2345f4 shows the VyOS NAT source rule (masquerade for 10.50.10.0/24 out eth1) being committed. cmd-a27bde5dbbf8419d shows the rule present in the live nft ruleset. cmd-0a22fe22715047d1 shows its packet counter incremented to 6 packets after real end-to-end traffic, directly confirming the rule was hit.

requirements.requirement: Second SNAT hop occurs on node2 (OPNsense) as traffic enters lan-b, and node4 records the connection as arriving from node2's lan-b address rather than node3 or node1
requirements.summary: cmd-bcd403b5a36f4af9 shows the corrected outbound SNAT rule (source 10.50.20.0/24 -> opt2 address) active in pf. cmd-1f93c608ebaf4842 shows matching pf NAT counters incrementing (26 packets, 5 states) concurrent with the real request. cmd-6a87cc71aa8740a9 directly shows node4's HTTP access log recording the client IP as 10.50.30.254, which is node2's lan-b address (confirmed by cmd-9ced37d7113a450f), not node3 (10.50.10.12) or node1 (10.50.20.1).

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: node1 baseline, restart, changed boot identity, and recovery
requirements.summary: cmd-e69e65be12e046ed captures pre-restart boot_id and cmd-a27bde5dbbf8419d shows the working NAT/route config beforehand. cmd-f3b2622146ad4c5f acknowledges the reboot; cmd-2fe524545c314d45 shows a changed boot_id after reconnect. cmd-be580e87dc2945dc shows interfaces/routes restored and pings succeeding, and cmd-b6c54f6137844040 shows the end-to-end HTTP path working again post-restart.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: node2 baseline, restart, changed boot identity, and recovery
requirements.summary: cmd-840048035a6742ac and cmd-d48bae2b58ac470c capture pre-restart boot time and healthy pf/forwarding/NAT state. cmd-453f5ba9651c4883 shows the reboot causing connection closure (acknowledgement); cmd-c7c8a4bc36554656 shows a changed kern.boottime after reconnect. cmd-7857c30f27734048 confirms interfaces, pf, NAT rule, and forwarding all restored, and cmd-a93c01929b4b497f shows the end-to-end HTTP path succeeding post-restart.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: node3 baseline, restart, changed boot identity, and recovery
requirements.summary: cmd-2f79fd808c5a4fef captures pre-restart boot_id. cmd-d1e895839743477e shows reboot closing the connection (acknowledgement). cmd-da42868b208e4fe6 shows a changed boot_id after reconnect. cmd-927bad91b91341d4 shows the persistent ifcfg-eth1/route restored and a successful end-to-end curl to node4:8080 post-restart.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: node4 baseline, restart, changed boot identity, and recovery
requirements.summary: cmd-99906ce9538a489f captures the pre-restart boot_id. cmd-4ddcda4be1d64f68 acknowledges the reboot and cmd-6289463fb02e4e20 shows a changed boot_id after reconnect. cmd-168559182db24adb confirms the persistent ifcfg-eth1 and firewalld port rule survived automatically, but the HTTP server itself did not recover on its own: it was run as a foreground nohup job rather than a persistent service, so it was not listening after reboot and required manual intervention (cmd-1f73bd6cd0674241 timed out attempting to relaunch it, cmd-e70c7fba48724b46 finally got it running). The end-to-end path was only restored after this manual step (cmd-4e6fce28f8ab452b, cmd-fd21e34f834a4884), so the 'service state' leg of the restart protocol was not demonstrated as self-healing.

overall_summary: The double-NAT path is directly demonstrated end-to-end: node4's HTTP access log records the connection as arriving from 10.50.30.254 (node2's lan-b address), not node3 or node1, with both SNAT hops confirmed live and incrementing packet counters concurrent with the real request. The provider-wide restart protocol was executed and evidenced for all four nodes with pre/post boot-identity changes and restored configuration, but node4's HTTP service was a non-persistent foreground process that did not survive reboot automatically and needed manual relaunching, so that leg of the restart protocol is only partially demonstrated as self-healing (this does not affect the core task outcome, since HTTP-service persistence across reboot was not part of the public task contract).
limitations: node4's HTTP server was run as an ad hoc foreground/nohup Python process rather than a managed service, so post-restart 'service recovery' required manual re-launch rather than being demonstrated as automatic; this is only a gap in the independent restart-evidence protocol, not in the public task contract.
Minor unreverted diagnostic residue (log files, /tmp/www) was left on node2, node3, and node4 after the session; low severity and does not affect functional correctness.

node3's own pre-restart 'healthy baseline' evidence relies on boot_id capture plus earlier/later end-to-end curl tests rather than a curl test taken immediately before its reboot, though this is a minor gap given surrounding evidence.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands were tied to satisfying the core NAT-path requirement or to correcting earlier missteps during empirical topology discovery (e.g., node1's initial eth1/eth2 address swap in cmd-29314e4c8a424421 was corrected in cmd-1122a3898ad84932 once real wiring was confirmed; node2's pf was briefly disabled for diagnosis in cmd-190d55258bc64e54 and re-enabled in cmd-358c065e402f458b, a bounded and fully reverted low-risk mutation). The many tcpdump captures and ping sweeps across all four nodes were read-only diagnostics used to determine actual L2 wiring, not unnecessary mutations. Minor unreverted residue exists: debug/log files left in /tmp on node2, node3 (eth1capture.log), and node4 (eth1.log, http.log, /tmp/www) after the session; these are low-risk leftover artifacts rather than damaging changes. The final NAT rule schema iteration on node2 (multiple base64-script config.xml edits in cmd-d27fa7f851844cd9, cmd-2b720cf2dfe742d8, cmd-bcd403b5a36f4af9) reflects legitimate trial-and-error to reach a working, retained configuration rather than an abandoned experiment. No destructive, broad, or security-weakening mutations were observed; firewalld and pf rules were only opened as narrowly as required for the task.
